I’m excited to share a milestone from MerLean: a research paper in spectral graph theory generated end-to-end by our AI research system, with every step of the main result verified by the Lean 4 proof assistant and the mathematical argument reviewed by human experts. Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity with 2(n−2) Edges: The Large Vertex Number Case

Algebraic connectivity measures how robustly a network is connected — it governs how well networks synchronize and resist being cut apart. In 2015, Kolokolnikov conjectured that among all networks on n nodes with exactly 2(n−2) links, one specific design, K(2, n−2), is the best possible.

Our paper proves it for every n ≥ 123, and the accompanying Lean formalization closes the conjecture entirely — every n ≥ 4. The proof ends in a pincer: one criterion forces a short cycle in any would-be counterexample, another forbids exactly those cycles, and the two collide once n ≥ 123. See formalization.yaml. The proof was discovered formally first — by agents (Fable + Opus + Lean 4) under our MerLean harness, an 18-day campaign producing 163,000 lines of verified Lean — then translated back into a human-readable paper and reviewed by human experts, reversing the usual informal-to-formal workflow.

MerLean is an evidence-based auto-research system for (applied) math and theoretical research. Agents work over a graph memory mirroring the Lean 4 dependency structure, and autonomously run Python numerical experiments to probe directions and test counterexamples: numerics propose; Lean disposes.
https://merleanprover.com/
